chronology.reason: Un-audited. Extraction carries many external Western intervals; native reign witnesses retained; no Western years invented or cleared by guesswork.

notes.note: The extraction assigns Western intervals to all 253 person records, usually marked as external or inferred. Those years are not supplied by this chapter and this source review does not approve any of them. Preserve the native reign-era and relative-date witnesses and submit every Western interval to the independent date-audit workflow.
Precise native witnesses include Xianning 4 咸寧四年, Taikang 6 太康六年, Yuankang 8 元康八年, Xianhe 2 咸和二年, Taiyuan 20 太元二十年, and Yixi 2 義熙二年. Keep these source strings; no Western conversion is asserted here.

The fixed ancient years attached to legendary and early figures are external conventions, not chapter evidence. Several duplicates also disagree, notably Liuxia Hui p009 versus p120. Treat these as unresolved research claims rather than accepted chronology.

Several stored intervals do not match their own sourceDate labels: p040 extends Xianning to 290; p046 extends Taishi to 290; p235 begins 'early Yixi' in 395; p241 uses 334-340 for Xianhe; and p242 labels a 365-427 lifespan-like span as Yixi. These require fresh source review and must not be normalized by guesswork.

extractionIssues.details: Continuous or clearly repeated individuals are split across records. Definite same-person groups include Xia Tong p014/p018/p250; Fan Can p041/p060; Fan Qiao p048/p050; Qiao Xiu p003/p125; Sun Deng p005/p247; Dong Jing p010/p248; Wu Zixu p036/p251; Jia Chong p028/p252; Song Xian p196/p253; Guo Yu p206/p212; Dai Kui p224/p233; and Tao Qian p242/p244. Recurring canonical people are also duplicated, including Confucius p001/p024/p066/p178/p210, Xunzi p002/p071, Yao p012/p033/p168, Shun p013/p034, Qu Yuan p015/p039, Liuxia Hui p009/p120, Sima Yan p046/p087, Zhang Hua p062/p081, Wang Dao p108/p137, Yu Liang p149/p159, Yu Yi p150/p160, Shi Le p164/p183, Shi Hu p165/p184, Fu Jian p190/p192/p213, and Zhuangzi p072/p180/p202.
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Merge only source-supported same individuals, preserving all attestations, names, claims, relationships, and date evidence. Do not merge generic or merely similar names.

extractionIssues.details: Named or title-identified people in the source are absent as records or attestations: Liang Hong and Guan Ning (s0122); Li Quan 李銓 (s0158); Xu Meng 許猛 (s0223); the Prince of Yan 燕王 (s0224, retain source-form if unresolved); Han founder Liu Bang 漢祖 (s0270); Li Xiang 李驤 (s0428); Xiao Jing 蕭敬 (s0432); Zhai Fasi 翟法賜 (s0459); Master Chisong 赤松, paired with Wang Qiao in 松喬 (s0504); Gai Gong 蓋公 (s0535); Qian Lou 黔婁 (s0545); Wei Hua 韋華 (s0612); Zhang Xing 張興 and Duanmu Gan 幹木 (s0638); Meng Gongming 孟公明 (s0662/s0668/s0670); Xin Zhang 辛章 (s0673); Zhang Dayu 張大豫 (s0674); Suo Gu 索嘏 (s0678/s0681); Peng Hezheng 彭和正 and Zhang Tianci 張天錫 (s0701); Wang Ya 王雅 (s0757); Zhang Ye 張野, Yang Songling 羊松齡, and Pang Zun 寵遵 (s0834); Pang Tongzhi 龐通之 (s0839); and Liuxia Hui 柳禽/展禽 (s0860).
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Add conservative source-form records or attestations and link to an existing canonical person only when identity is definite. In particular, s0860 belongs with existing Liuxia Hui rather than a new Liu Qin/Liu Ling.

extractionIssues.details: The extraction omits explicitly present unnamed people needed for complete mention and relationship coverage: Zhang Hua's son sent to Lu Sheng; Dong Yang's wife; Gong Zhuang's father and uncle; Liu Linzhi's father; Fan Xuan's elder brother and that brother's daughter, who became Dai Kui's wife; Tao Qian's wife and children; and the student and two sons involved at Tao Qian's death.
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Represent the source-form anonymous people and attach only the relationships directly stated in these units.

extractionIssues.details: p210 gives Confucius a surface and attestation at s0739, but the Chinese says 二本 ('the two roots/foundations') and does not mention Confucius.
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Remove the s0739 Confucius surface and attestation while retaining his genuine mentions elsewhere.

extractionIssues.details: p248 assigns Dong Jing a surface and claim in s0859 solely because the defective idiomatic field inserts his name. The Chinese s0859 concerns Sun Deng; Dong Jing begins in s0860. Conversely, s0860 fails to attest Liuxia Hui because 柳禽 was mistranslated.
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Remove Dong Jing from s0859, keep him at s0860, and add s0860 to the existing Liuxia Hui person after the translation repair.

extractionIssues.details: p060 is a separate Fan Can record whose supposed Chinese personal name is 武威, but Wuwei is the office/geographic title by which Fan Can was known in context, not another person.
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Merge p060 into Fan Can and store Wuwei only as a source-appropriate office/title association.

extractionIssues.details: The extraction's all-durable-facts coverage claim is not met. Definite omissions include Zhu Chong's Erudite appointment; Fan Can's sequence of staff and court offices; Lu Sheng's editorial appointment; Guo Qi's and Wu Chao's appointments; Ren Xu's filial-and-incorrupt nomination, Gentleman of the Palace appointment, and commandery zhongzheng role; Sima Rui's later summons; Han Ji's Erudite appointment; Zhai Tang's and Zhai Zhuang's summonses; Xin Mi's Crown Prince Attendant and princely literary instructor appointments; Xia Tong's Grand Master of Ceremonies summons; Dai Kui's court and academy summonses; Gong Deng's Gentleman-in-Regular-Attendance office; Gong Xuanzhi and Dai Kui's joint appointments; and Tao Qian's provincial, military-staff, and editorial appointments.
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Add office/event claims from the cited units with exact source witnesses; distinguish offered, summoned, accepted, declined, and actually held offices.

extractionIssues.details: Existing claims lose source-critical participants or relationships: Gong Zhuang's uncle is omitted from Li Te's killings; Bing Yu is specifically Bing Yuan's great-grandson; Li Xiang is Li Xiong's uncle and Li Shou's father and joined the summons of Qiao Xiu; Xiao Jing joined Fan Ben's rebellion; and Fan Xuan gave his elder brother's daughter to Dai Kui as wife.
extractionIssues.recommendedAction: Repair these events and relationships after the corresponding translation fixes, retaining every named participant.

sourceReviewCoverage.summary: Reviewed all 869 units and both English fields, plus all 9 existing proposed repairs. Found 38 additional or refined definite translation repairs across 33 units; together with the nonduplicated existing proposals, 37 units have a definite translation defect and 832 do not. The extraction also has definite duplicate records, missing named and unnamed people, two false mentions, a title misread as a person name, and substantial missing office and relationship claims. All Western chronology remains unapproved pending independent date audit.
